chapter: Claude Hopkins, Fletcher Henderson and Fats Waller
title: Joining Hopkins at the Regal Theatre; theatres and two record sessions
summary: Mosley joins Hopkins in Chicago in summer 1934, plays theatres and makes two record sessions.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Where did you join Claude?
I joined Claude at the Regal Theatre in Chicago. That's 1934.
The summer of '34. The place that you played in St. Louis was an open air place, wasn't it?
Out in the open.
There was another place they tried but it didn't work out somehow, something happened that it didn't work out and only the big place, the big Club Plantation in St. Louis was the only one that--
I didn't play there.
I forget the name of the place where you played.
That's where I met Dizzy Dean.
So you're with Claude; Claude wasn't doing anything with theatres then, was he?
Yeah, he was in a lot of theatres.
It wasn't all black theatres either, was it?
No.
He played white theatres?
He played some white theatres.
And of course you made a couple of records--let's see the list, see if we got any records. We should show "Mandy"; we should show at least two.
This shows two sessions; I'm sure
I played two sessions.
You played two sessions with Claude.
I've got them here; I've got records.
I used to have one of those. You played solo on Mandy, I think.
"Do You Ever Think of Me" too.
Yeah. Weren't you on "Zozoi?"
No. I was on more than that.
You were on a couple of them. I know you made at least two sessions.
I was on two sessions with Claude. In fact, I've got--Mandy.
